properties.title: FlatASCEND: Autoregressive Clinical Sequence Generation with Continuous Time Prediction and Association-Based Pharmacological Testing

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Autoregressive clinical sequence model with continuous time prediction and a patient-level pharmacological association test.
GPT-2-style decoder with flat composite tokens, ALiBi, value-factored embeddings, a zero-inflated log-normal time head and free-running scheduled sampling, used with forced-intervention generation.

legacy_cells.B: FlatASCEND: Autoregressive Clinical Sequence Generation with Continuous Time Prediction and Association-Based Pharmacological Testing
legacy_cells.C: Sainsbury, Chris, Dong, Feng, Karwath, Andreas
legacy_cells.S: Can a patient-conditioned autoregressive EHR model generate multi-step clinical event and timing continuations, and do medication-conditioned trajectories reproduce known pharmacological association directions?
legacy_cells.T: MIMIC-IV v3.0: 424,974 admissions (303,920 after ≥20-token filtering); INSPECT: approximately 19,000 outpatient patients; eICU-CRD: 200,859 stays; proprietary development cohort: approximately 61,000 diabetes-registry patients.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Structured EHR event tokens (laboratory results, vital signs, medications, diagnoses, demographics/special tokens); inter-event time deltas
legacy_cells.AJ: GPT-2-style autoregressive transformer with ALiBi positional encoding
legacy_cells.AM: Additive fusion: content-token embeddings plus a time embedding from log(1 + Δt)
legacy_cells.AX: Prompt-shuffle ablation: randomly permuted prompt tokens and compared pharmacological effects with ordered patient histories; mechanistic-control effects fell 2.0–2.2×, while the confounding-driven insulin–glucose effect was 0.9×.
legacy_cells.BD: Medication class or individual-drug token; forced at Δt = 0; same-class medications suppressed during generation.
legacy_cells.BF: During generation, all medications from the forced drug's therapeutic class are suppressed to prevent cross-arm contamination.
legacy_cells.BL: Inter-event time Δt; zero for within-visit events and otherwise sampled from a continuous log-normal component (time intervals reported in days).
legacy_cells.BN: Factored measure-identity and ordinal-level embeddings, with an ordinal earth-mover's-distance auxiliary loss to bias ordinal relationships across measures.
legacy_cells.BP: Maximum sequence length: 512 tokens for MIMIC-IV; 1,024 for INSPECT and the development dataset.
legacy_cells.BS: Autoregressively generated clinical event tokens and associated inter-event time deltas.
legacy_cells.BT: Weight-tied content head projecting to vocabulary logits; zero-inflated log-normal time head predicting (logit_z, μ, log σ).
legacy_cells.BV: Content cross-entropy + 0.5 × zero-inflated log-normal time loss + 0.25 × ordinal earth-mover's-distance loss.
legacy_cells.CA: Single NVIDIA A100 (80 GB); mixed-precision bfloat16 autocast.
legacy_cells.CD: 200 generated tokens per patient in the trajectory-fidelity evaluation.
legacy_cells.CG: 200–500 independent generated trajectories per patient per arm in pharmacological testing; the main MIMIC-IV incident-user analysis used N = 500 patients per comparison.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported results (source excerpt): Standard unconditional distributional metrics (Jaccard similarity 0.889–0.954) do not distinguish FlatASCEND from trivial baselines; the model’s value lies inconditionalgeneration from patient-specific clinical prefixes. A prompt-shuffle ablation provides direct supporting evidence: patient-specific conditioning amplifies mechanistic pharmacological effects (2.0–2.2× for steroid→ glucose and diuretic→ potassium) while leaving confounding-driven associations unchanged (0.9× for insulin→ glucose). Direct preference optimisation with surrogate reward destroys all pre-existing correct associations (3/3 to 0/3), illustrating reward exploitation when the reward and evaluation share an outcome domain.
legacy_cells.FR: Forced intervention/control continuations from the same prefix demonstrate model-based comparisons, not identified clinical treatment effects. Only 4/10 pharmacological comparisons recover correct mechanistic direction; DPO destroys all three previously correct evaluated associations, illustrating model/reward exploitation.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Use patient-prefix shuffling, trivial generators and pharmacological direction checks; audit surrogate-reward optimization for lost valid associations.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF text, pp. 1–22: title/abstract; Introduction; Results §§2.1–2.2.7 and Tables 1–8; Discussion §§3.1–3.4; Limitations §3.3; Methods §§4.1–4.5; AI Technology Disclosure; Ethics and Data Access; Code and Data Availability; Supplementary Tables S1–S4; References. Tables were inspected throughout; some extracted table rows/cells are line-wrapped or misaligned. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Complete local PDF text was read, and A:I were left untouched. Core extraction uses explicit Methods/Results evidence. Some extracted table cells are line-wrapped or misaligned; no ambiguous table-only values were used. Action-conditioned drug-token comparisons are classified as associational, not causal; no planning/control or clinical deployment is demonstrated. Evidence QA: 36/49 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (73.5%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 40 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 9 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All 22 physical PDF pages were read as extracted text; pages 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, and 20 (Tables 1-8, Supplementary Table S4, Supplementary Figure S1) were directly inspected via rendered PNGs during Phase E repair.
The legacy row was read from the root workbook (read only). Saved API drafts for B083 were not opened.
The repository stated in the paper is private and was not inspected.
Only 4 of 10 incident-user comparisons recover a correct mechanistic direction (4 wrong due to confounding by indication); no causal identification is attempted.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. No independent human review.
notes: FlatASCEND is a 14.5M-parameter GPT-2-style EHR generator with flat composite tokens and a zero-inflated log-normal time head. Unconditional metrics (Jaccard 0.889 to 0.954) are matched by trivial baselines, and zero-shot transfer to eICU-CRD degrades (Jaccard 0.682, recovered to 0.820 after adaptation). A forced-intervention test on MIMIC-IV recovers 4 of 10 mechanistic directions with 4 wrong, and a prompt-shuffle ablation halves mechanistic effects. The authors state the associations are observational. Classified L2, core. Source points: no architectural ablation on open data, confounding, private repository.
